chapter: Handedness and Gene Austin in California
title: Afternoon band at the Grove and Eddie Miller's phone call
summary: The union penalty is settled, he plays afternoons with fiddles and viola, and Eddie Miller hears his mellophone on the radio.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: around $35 a week and I told them they didn't believe me. I told them I said well I didn't lie to you so far why should I lie to you about that? So it wound up that they fined Coco $250 and they fined a bass player $250 and Austin $1,000 and $1,100 they had to pay back. They didn't fined me a dime. So I got you know just by telling the truth I got by without having to pay anything. So with this place in the back that we played in the afternoon we played from 12 to 3. So we had Coco, myself, the bass and we had two fills and a viola and had Stan Reitzman on piano. Stan was just club dating around. He had been working with Hank Hal Halstead you know and they weren't doing anything. So I got Stan to play piano and Austin didn't come there at all. He didn't sing at all in the afternoon. So we worked out things just to have the fiddles and the viola just play sustain things and figures and things like that and we had to broadcast for half an hour too. And I'd take courses on the mellow phone and on the cornet and Coco would take courses on the guitar and the piano see. So we had enough jazz there for the other. And the other guys just saw them. So the phone rings one day and Ed Wade had called me and the phone said somebody wants to talk to you. You want to talk to me. So I get on the phone. The minute I open my mouth Eddie Miller hollers I knew it was you. It couldn't be nobody else but you Pollock's band had just flew in. That's where they broke up. Of course out there then. And they had flew in and they happened to turn the radio on in the hotel you know. And they heard this music and they heard the mellow phone. They knew it wasn't there. It couldn't be anybody else but me. And when they heard where it was coming from he called me there.
